auth.v1.AssistantKeyPreset.description:
AssistantKeyPreset is a fixed permission set for a Polyester AI assistant
 key. SetAssistantKeys turns it into an API policy of the key's main account,
 named after the preset, so the policy and the key need only the set's one
 step-up proof. No preset ever allows a money-out action (EXTERNAL_WITHDRAW,
 INTERNAL_TRANSFER, MANAGE_ADDRESS_BOOK, MANAGE_AUTO_WITHDRAW), API-key or
 policy management, or any action that weakens account security.

auth.v1.PolicyAction.description:
PolicyAction is a high-level permission that can be granted by a policy.
 Product actions apply to sub-account and API-key policies, and their
 write-style actions also grant the matching read visibility where needed by
 the product experience. Account permissions, each documented below as an
 account permission or a main-account permission, apply to API-key policies
 only: a sub-account policy refuses them. Each account permission grants
 exactly the calls it names and never implies another permission. A
 main-account permission is honored only for an API key scoped to the main
 account; a key scoped to a sub-account is refused even when its policy
 grants it. Admin permissions, documented below, apply to API-key policies
 only and are honored only for an admin API key. An API key without a policy
 has no permission at all.
auth.v1.PolicyAction.title: PolicyAction

removed.description:
True when the caller no longer has access to this sub-account, for
 example after its owner removed the caller as a member: remove the
 sub-account from the caller's list. Only real-time updates set it;
 responses list only sub-accounts the caller can access. A change of the
 caller's role or access does not change revision or updated_at, so
 real-time updates deliver such changes in order and each one applies as
 it arrives. Ending access also ends the caller's subscriptions to this
 sub-account's real-time channels, and can, rarely, also end a
 subscription made after access was granted again. When the server ends a
 subscription to one of this sub-account's channels while the latest
 update lists this sub-account with a role and removed false, subscribe
 again: access is checked again on subscribe.
removed.title: removed

spotMarketScope.description:
Market-level scope for spot markets. When ALL, spot_markets is returned
 for display only and is not enforced.
spotMarketScope.title: spot_market_scope

spotMarkets.description: Allowed spot markets for this sub-account.
spotMarkets.title: spot_markets

tradingHalted.description:
When true, new orders and exposure-increasing order or trigger changes are
 rejected regardless of other settings. Existing orders and triggers may
 still be canceled or paused by an otherwise authorized caller.
tradingHalted.title: trading_halted

auth.v1.SubaccountRole.title: SubaccountRole

ledger.read.v1.AssetBalance.description:
Fixed-size representation for balances (for Protobuf/WS clients).
 Uses common U128 messages for amounts to keep schema tidy and consistent.

assetId.description:
Public unified asset id. Resolve symbol from SpotConfig; U128 amounts in
 this message always use fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.
assetId.title: asset_id

available.description:
Amount currently available for new trading activity at fixed 18-decimal
 ledger scale. This value already accounts for active reservations.
available.title: available

funding.description: Funding balance at fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.
funding.title: funding

fundingRevision.description:
Opaque monotonic revision for the funding value. Higher means newer; zero
 means no funding state has been observed. Trading values have no
 revision: their position is (trading_epoch, trading_sequence).
fundingRevision.title: funding_revision

reserved.description: Reserved amount in the trading bucket at fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.
reserved.title: reserved

trading.description: Trading balance at fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.
trading.title: trading

ledger.read.v1.AssetBalance.title: AssetBalance

ledger.read.v1.GetBalancesResponse.description:
GetBalancesResponse is the account's balances with the position of its
 Trading values.

 The Trading values of every asset are one atomic cut: all are taken at the
 single position (trading_epoch, trading_sequence) the response names, never
 a mix of two positions, and never at a position older than one the balance
 stream already published. The Funding values carry their own
 funding_revision and are not part of that position.

balances.description:
One entry for every supported unified asset, including assets with zero
 balances. Sorted by available trading amount (highest first), then by
 asset symbol alphabetically.
balances.title: balances

tradingAppliedThroughTsNs.description:
Every Trading transfer of the account whose ts_ns is at or below this
 value is applied in these balances, a receipt within trading_epoch.
 While a transfer of the account could not be applied, this value stays
 below it, until a later balance of that asset includes it; it never
 passes a transfer that is not applied. Nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).
tradingAppliedThroughTsNs.title: trading_applied_through_ts_ns

tradingEpoch.description:
The Trading numbering the balances' Trading values are in. It changes
 when the numbering restarts: then reload. Compare it only for equality;
 its value has no order. Zero, with trading_sequence zero, when the
 account has no Trading balances yet.
tradingEpoch.title: trading_epoch

tradingSequence.description:
The Trading sequence the balances' Trading values are at, within
 trading_epoch: apply the balance stream's Trading updates from
 trading_sequence + 1 on (see BalanceUpdate).
tradingSequence.title: trading_sequence

ledger.read.v1.GetBalancesResponse.title: GetBalancesResponse

polyester.type.v1.U128.description:
U128 represents an unsigned 128-bit integer as two fixed64 parts:
 value = (hi << 64) | lo.

 Public amount fields that use U128, including ledger balances and fields
 named amount_e18, use fixed 18-decimal scale unless their field comment says
 otherwise. U128 can also carry raw identifiers, such as a withdraw nonce; do
 not apply decimal scaling to those fields.
polyester.type.v1.U128.title: U128

ApiKeySignatureAuth.name: X-API-SIGNATURE

ApiKeyTimestampAuth.description: Time the request was signed, in Unix milliseconds. An API-key request sends it with X-API-KEY-ID and X-API-SIGNATURE.
ApiKeyTimestampAuth.name: X-API-TIMESTAMP

Call this API from the broker's backend, never from a browser or mobile app. The broker's members create, rotate and revoke keys through the QuickSwap broker API, and a key may rotate itself.
